text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000589 bills 99215 far above risk-adjusted expectation across every complexity band except 5+, but documentation is too thin to confirm or refute upcoding.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The billing pattern raises concern because the elevated 99215 share holds even for patients with 0 or 1 chronic conditions. Sampled examples include C0312390 (rash, no conditions), C0312408 (UTI, age 18) and C0312575 (follow-up Z09). These look like routine visits billed at the highest level. In contrast, the provider's 99215 share in the 5+ condition band is at or below the all-provider rate, which is the opposite of what a genuinely sicker panel would usually show. On the other side, the few documented 99215 claims all supported the billed level, including low-complexity claim C0312901. However, with only 4 documented 99215s the rule check deems this too few to judge. The 5 of 15 moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab or test line on the claim are weak evidence that notes may be templated or inflated, not proof. A reviewer should first request full charts for the low-complexity 99215 sample, especially the zero-condition visits such as C0312390, C0312408, C0312575, C0312802 and C0312641. They should check those notes for cloned MDM language and for whether the time or data elements are actually supported."}
